{{nihongo|'''Hasedera (Nagano)'''|長谷寺}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

[[ja:長谷寺 (長野市)]]

{{wikidata link|Q11653682|ja|長谷寺 (長野市)|grok=none|check_date=2026-05-29}}

'''Hasedera''' (はせでら) is a {{ill|Buddhist temple|Q5393308|qid=Q5393308}} of the {{ill|Shingon-shū Chisan-ha|Q674374|qid=Q674374}} of {{ill|Shingon Buddhism|Q550182|qid=Q550182}} in Shinonoi Shionosaki, {{ill|Nagano (city)|Q128849|qid=Q128849}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}}. Its mountain name is Kinpōzan. It is commonly called '''Shinano Hasedera'''.

Among the many Hasedera temples across Japan, it is one of the three called the "Three Great Hasedera of Japan" (Yamato, Kamakura, and Shinano), together with the {{ill|Hase-dera (disambiguation)|de|Hase-dera|fr|Hase-dera|ja|長谷寺 (曖昧さ回避)|nl|Hase-dera|zh|長谷寺 (消歧義)|qid=Q1588189|lt=Hasedera}} of {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato}} and {{ill|Kamakura|Q200267|qid=Q200267}}.

=== History ===
Temple tradition states that in the era of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|Q329761|qid=Q329761}} (629-641), Hakujō (also called Haku-suke), a sixth-generation descendant of {{ill|Emperor Ingyō|Q349258|qid=Q349258}}, who had been exiled to this region in his grandfather's generation and settled here, received an oracle from {{ill|Amitābha|Q236242|qid=Q236242}} of {{ill|Zenkō-ji|arz|زينكو جى|bcl|Zenkō-ji|de|Zenkō-ji|el|Ζένκο-τζι|es|Zenko-ji|eu|Zenkō-ji|fa|زنکو-جی|fr|Zenkō-ji|gan|善光寺|hu|Zenkódzsi|ja|善光寺|jv|Zenko-ji|ko|젠코지|nl|Zenko-ji|ru|Дзэнкодзи|sv|Zenkō-ji|uk|Монастир Дзенко|zh|善光寺|qid=Q189640}} in Shinano and invited an Eleven-faced Kannon from Hatsuseyama in {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato}}, which became the origin of this temple. (The exact year is unknown; even the temple website lists only the Asuka period.)

The {{ill|Hase-dera|arz|هاس ديرا (ساكوراى, نارا, اليابان)|de|Hase-dera (Sakurai)|el|Ναός Χάσε-Ντέρα|fr|Hase-dera (Sakurai)|gan|長谷寺|ja|長谷寺|tr|Hase-dera|uz|Haze-dera|zh|長谷寺|qid=Q1457787}} at Hatsuse in Yamato (Sakurai, Nara Prefecture) is said to have begun when Dōmyō of {{ill|Kawara-dera|fr|Kawara-dera|ja|川原寺|qid=Q3194342}} founded an original Hasedera in {{ill|686|Q30619|qid=Q30619}} (Shuchō 1), and in {{ill|AD 727|ab|727|af|727|als|727|am|727 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|727|ar|727|ast|727|az|727|azb|۷۲۷ (میلادی)|be|727|be_x_old|727|bg|727|bn|৭২৭|bpy|মারি ৭২৭|br|727|bs|727.|ca|727|cdo|727 nièng|ceb|727|ckb|٧٢٧|crh|727|cs|727|cv|727|cy|727|da|727|de|727|el|727|eml|727|eo|727|es|727|et|727|eu|727|fa|۷۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|727|fo|727|fr|727|fy|727|ga|727|gan|727年|gd|727|gl|727|he|727|hi|727|hr|727.|ht|727 (almanak jilyen)|hu|727|hy|727|id|727|io|727|is|727|it|727|ja|727年|jv|727|ka|727|kaa|727|kk|727 жыл|ko|727년|la|727|lb|727|lij|727|lmo|727|lt|727 m.|map_bms|727|mdf|727|mg|727|mhr|727|mk|727|mr|इ.स. ७२७|mrj|727 и|ms|727|mzn|۷۲۷|nah|727|nap|727|nds|727|new|सन् ७२७|nl|727|nn|727|no|727|nrm|727|nso|727|oc|727|or|୭୨୭|os|727-æм аз|pl|727|pnb|727|pt|727|qu|727|ro|727|ru|727 год|rue|727|sa|७२७|scn|727|sd|727ع|sh|727.|si|727|sk|727|sl|727|smn|727|sq|727|sr|727|su|727|sv|727|sw|727|tg|Соли 727|th|พ.ศ. 1270|tk|727|tl|727|tly|727|tr|727|tt|727 ел|uk|727|ur|727ء|uz|727|vec|727|vi|727|war|727|wuu|727年|xmf|727|zh|727年|zh_classical|七二七年|zh_min_nan|727 nî|zh_yue|727年|qid=Q23557}} (Jinki 4) Tokudō carved an Eleven-faced Kannon and opened the current Hasedera. While the Yamato Hasedera certainly existed from the Nara period, this foundation story is traditional lore; therefore, how far the origin tradition of Shinano Hasedera reflects historical fact is uncertain.

From the mountain behind the temple, a bronze {{ill|kyōzutsu|ja|経筒|qid=Q11606503}} inscribed {{ill|1151|Q19642|qid=Q19642}} (Ninpei 1) has been excavated, showing that in that year a monk titled {{ill|Daishi|ja|大師|zh|大師|qid=Q10935264}} buried copies of the ''{{ill|Lotus Sutra|Q861212|qid=Q861212|lt=Myōhō Rengekyō}}'' and ''{{ill|The Amitāyus Sutra|bn|দীর্ঘ সুখাবতীব্যূহ সূত্র|fr|Sūtra de Vie-Infinie|id|Sutra Kehidupan Tanpa Batas|ja|無量寿経|ko|무량수경|no|Sutraen om evig liv|ru|Большая Сукхавативьюха сутра|si|දීර්ඝ සුඛාවතීව්‍යූහ සූත්‍රය|sv|Den längre sukhāvatīvyūhaḥsūtran|vi|Vô Lượng Thọ kinh|wuu|无量寿经|zh|無量壽經|zh_classical|無量壽經|zh_yue|無量壽經|qid=Q6029801}}'' on Mt. Hase.

* {{ill|1181|Q19704|qid=Q19704}} ({{ill|Yōwa|Q729609|qid=Q729609}} 1): In the ''{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'', guardian Hase Shrine became a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}.
: Around this time, {{ill|Kakumyo Tayubo|Q11630332|qid=Q11630332}} (formerly military strategist of {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshinaka|Q1139202|qid=Q1139202}}, disciple of {{ill|Hōnen|Q507980|qid=Q507980}}, and companion of {{ill|Shinran|Q512934|qid=Q512934}}) founded Kōraku-ji near Hasedera.
* Around {{ill|1200|Q5224|qid=Q5224}} ({{ill|Shōji (era)|Q1199890|qid=Q1199890}} 2), "Hasedera Reigenki" was compiled.
* {{ill|1290|Q5552|qid=Q5552}} ({{ill|Shōō (Kamakura period)|ar|حقبة شو (كاماكورا)|de|Shōō|fa|شوئو (دوره کاماکورا)|fr|Ère Shōō|ia|Shoo|id|Shōō|ja|正応|ko|쇼오|ru|Сёо (Камакура)|simple|Shōō (Kamakura period)|sr|Шо (Камакура период)|sv|Shōō|tr|Shōō (Kamakura)|zh|正應|qid=Q1327371}} 3): By a revelatory dream of {{ill|Prince Hisaaki|Q715826|qid=Q715826}}, regent {{ill|Hōjō Sadatoki|Q3136681|qid=Q3136681}} had monk Shinkai restore Hasedera.
* {{ill|1346|Q6080|qid=Q6080}} (Southern court: Shohei 1, Northern court: Jōwa 2): tax-exempt fields of Hasedera are recorded in "Tenryu-ji documents."
: Around this time, "Sangoku Denki" was compiled and includes the Hakujō legend (Vol. 5, No. 30 "Shinshu Sarashina-gun Hakukeio no Koto").
* {{ill|1400|Q6108|qid=Q6108}} ({{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} 7): warfare occurred around Hasedera due to the {{ill|Battle of Ōtō|Q11433918|qid=Q11433918}}.
* Early Edo period: 15 koku of temple lands were donated by the Tokugawa shogunate.
* {{ill|1701|Q6814|qid=Q6814}} ({{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 14): Koyasu Hall constructed.
* {{ill|1713|Q6873|qid=Q6873}} ({{ill|Shōtoku (era)|Q1193848|qid=Q1193848|lt=Shotoku}} 3): Kannon Hall rebuilt.
* {{ill|1776|Q7703|qid=Q7703}} ({{ill|An'ei|Q1193910|qid=Q1193910|lt=An'ei}} 5): Niō gate constructed.
* {{ill|1802|Q6883|qid=Q6883}} ({{ill|Kyōwa|Q960763|qid=Q960763}} 2): bell-tower gate constructed.
* {{ill|1805|Q6898|qid=Q6898}} ({{ill|Bunka|Q1373146|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka}} 2): Jūō Hall constructed; stone foundation collapsed in the Zenkoji earthquake.
* {{ill|1847|Q7644|qid=Q7644}} ({{ill|Kōka|Q1325317|qid=Q1325317}} 4): temple buildings damaged in the {{ill|1847 Zenkoji earthquake|ar|زلزال زينكوجي 1847|es|Terremoto de Zenko-ji de 1847|fr|Séisme de 1847 à Nagano|ja|善光寺地震|ko|젠코지 지진|zh|善光寺地震|qid=Q11418893|lt=Great Zenkoji earthquake}}.
* {{ill|1863|Q7701|qid=Q7701}} ({{ill|Bunkyū|Q730266|qid=Q730266}} 3): kuri (priests' quarters) constructed.
* {{ill|1866|Q7712|qid=Q7712}} ({{ill|Keiō|Q776775|qid=Q776775}} 2): founder hall constructed.
* Showa period: temple buildings repaired; sutra container excavated.
* Heisei period: Kannon Hall, main hall, and kuri renovated; sutra repository built.

=== Events ===
* {{ill|January 1|Q2150|qid=Q2150}}-{{ill|January 5|Q2202|qid=Q2202}} - New Year and first-goma austerities
* {{ill|January 7|Q2228|qid=Q2228}} - Nanakusa protective seal distribution
* {{ill|January 18|Q2265|qid=Q2265}} - First Kannon exorcism prayer meeting
* {{ill|March 15|Q2403|qid=Q2403}} - Nirvana assembly and picture explanation
* {{ill|March 21|Q2433|qid=Q2433}} - Spring equinox assembly and official portrait offering
* {{ill|April 18|Q2521|qid=Q2521}} - Spring grand festival and great Prajna sutra reading
* {{ill|August 9|Q2782|qid=Q2782}} - Ugusai 33 Lanterns (Sanjosa)
* {{ill|August 10|Q2779|qid=Q2779}} - Segaki service
* {{ill|September 23|Q2888|qid=Q2888}} - Autumn equinox assembly
* {{ill|December 12|Q2369|qid=Q2369}} - Hōon-kō
* {{ill|December 18|Q2438|qid=Q2438}} - Year-end Kannon rite
* {{ill|December 31|Q2912|qid=Q2912}} - New Year's Eve service and two-year visit
* 18th of each month - day associated with Eleven-faced Kannon
* Second Sunday each month - sutra-copying gathering

=== Other events ===
* Shinano pilgrimage association - regularly conducts pilgrimages to Kannon sacred sites such as Saigoku, Bandō, Chichibu, and Shinano, as well as the {{ill|Shikoku Pilgrimage|Q1972399|qid=Q1972399}}.
* O-ekitoki (picture sermon) - explanation of the Śākyamuni nirvana painting. In addition to March 15, it is also given at this temple and as traveling lectures regardless of sect.
